result: Shamsi rejected all four, and noted that her standard rose as the builds improved, so verdicts no longer measure progress. No build used a sidebar, and the explanation of the figures became a footnote under the cards on all sections, both from the docs added after round 7. No build used the sort bar. The category list went behind show more (A, B), into an accordion at the bottom (C), or was left out (D); Shamsi wants the whole list tucked away and shown whole when needed. Refresh was not grouped with the updated line, and only C gave it an icon.

A.notes: Twelve rules on tokens, one class with no rule; copies the show-more script; a select, a checkbox and a Sort button.

B.notes: Eight rules on tokens; show more inline; Sort by and Order selects.

C.notes: Two rules on tokens. Did not open its pages in a browser.

D.notes: Six rules on tokens. Left out the category list and the Refresh on all sections; Refresh moved to the header tools.

patterns: No sidebar in any build (three of four in round 7).
All four put the explanation of the figures in a line below the cards on all sections, following Where secondary content goes.

No build used the sort bar. Agents said reversing needs JavaScript, or that the docs offer a Sort by select; the docs had two sort patterns and no rule for choosing, and the routing table pointed only at table headers.
Show more on the category list in A and B came from the docs' own example ('the first eight categories').
All four put 'About these charts' in an accordion above the list, which the docs allowed ('above it when it is one closed row').
No build used a popover or a modal: the Modals page said a modal is not for information that does not block the reader.
Primary content top at 1440 by 900: all sections 180 to 264px; activity charts 500 to 624px (placeholders now in cards, and the category list or sort form above them).

Predictions: 1 right (no sidebar). 2 wrong (no sort bar). 3 partly right (the one-line note became a footnote; the chart explanation still went in an accordion). 4 not measurable: Shamsi stopped using verdicts as a measure.
findings: Two sort patterns with no rule for choosing between them: no build used the sort bar.
The docs' own examples steered the builds: show more for categories, and an accordion above the list.
The docs ruled out a modal for content the reader asks to see, and pointed a long list at show more, so no build tried a popover or a modal.
next: Say when to use a sort bar and route to it; group Refresh, with its icon, with the updated line; point a list or explanation the reader opens when needed at a popover or a modal; switch the review to best and worst picks; run round 9.
